scams.name: The Chennai Central Auto Commission Loop
scams.tldr: You step out of Chennai Central station, bags in hand, and an auto-rickshaw driver quotes you ₹50 to your hotel.
scams.description: You step out of Chennai Central station, bags in hand, and an auto-rickshaw driver quotes you ₹50 to your hotel. The number is suspiciously low — a real meter ride would be at least ₹150 — but you are tired and the price is right. You hop in.
scams.avoidance: Use Ola or Uber for transparent pricing and GPS-tracked routes. If taking an auto, negotiate the fare upfront and insist the driver use the meter. Track your route on Google Maps and speak up immediately if the driver deviates. Never accept unsolicited shop recommendations from your driver. Pre-book airport transfers through your hotel for arrival peace of mind.
scams.location: Central Railway Station, Chennai Airport, T. Nagar, Marina Beach

scams.name: The Kapaleeshwarar Temple Blessing Shakedown
scams.tldr: You are admiring the gopuram at Kapaleeshwarar Temple in Mylapore when a man in priestly garments approaches.
scams.description: You are admiring the gopuram at Kapaleeshwarar Temple in Mylapore when a man in priestly garments approaches. Before you can react he places a garland of fragrant flowers around your neck and dabs a tilak on your forehead. He leads you to a side shrine, chants a quick blessing, and the moment lands as warm and unfamiliar at the same time.
scams.avoidance: Politely decline any unsolicited blessings or garlands by keeping your hands by your sides. Official temple priests never chase tourists outside the sanctum -- approach them yourself if interested. If you want a puja, ask at the temple office for official rates posted on notice boards. Never accept items placed in your hands or around your neck without agreeing first. Carry small bills so you can offer a modest donation and walk away confidently.
scams.location: Kapaleeshwarar Temple (Mylapore), Parthasarathy Temple, temples near Mahabalipuram

scams.name: The Marina Beach Parking Extortion
scams.tldr: You park along the strip near Marina Beach for a sunset walk.
scams.description: You park along the strip near Marina Beach for a sunset walk. As you step away from the car, a young man in a fluorescent vest appears from nowhere, slaps a handwritten 'ticket' on your windshield, and demands ₹100 for parking. He has no badge, no rate card, and no connection to any city authority — but in the moment it is easier to pay than argue.
scams.avoidance: Use the official Chennai Smart City parking app or look for metered spots. Ask to see an official ID and printed municipal rate card before paying. Take a photo of the attendant and their 'ticket' as documentation. If pressured, offer to call the Chennai traffic police helpline (103) on the spot. Park in established lots at malls or hotels nearby and walk to the beach.
scams.location: Marina Beach, Besant Nagar Beach, Elliot's Beach

scams.name: The T. Nagar Silk Saree Switcheroo
scams.tldr: You are shopping for silk sarees in T.
scams.description: You are shopping for silk sarees in T. Nagar — one of Chennai's most famous textile districts — and a shopkeeper unfolds a gorgeous Kanchipuram silk across the counter. He hands it to you to feel: the weight, the sheen, the slight crispness that distinguishes real Kanchipuram from anything synthetic. You agree on a price, he begins to wrap it in tissue paper while another staff member appears with chai and three more sarees to consider.
scams.avoidance: Do the burn test: real silk smells like burnt hair, synthetic smells like plastic -- ask to test a thread. Rub the fabric between your fingers -- genuine silk warms up, synthetic stays cool. Watch the packaging process closely and inspect the saree again before final payment. Shop at established government emporiums like Co-optex or VTB Silks with official certifications. Pay by card for a transaction trail and potential chargeback protection.
scams.location: T. Nagar, Pondy Bazaar, shops near Kapaleeshwarar Temple

scams.name: The Egmore Fake Tour Agent Vanish
scams.tldr: You find a travel agent on social media who offers a multi-day tour package to Mahabalipuram and Pondicherry at an incredible rate — air-conditioned car, hotel, guide, all for half the price of established agencies.
scams.description: You find a travel agent on social media who offers a multi-day tour package to Mahabalipuram and Pondicherry at an incredible rate — air-conditioned car, hotel, guide, all for half the price of established agencies. The Instagram page is professional, the messages are quick, and the WhatsApp confirmation looks legitimate. He asks for full payment by bank transfer to lock in the rate.
scams.avoidance: Book through established platforms like MakeMyTrip, verified TripAdvisor-listed operators, or your hotel. Never pay full amount upfront -- legitimate agencies accept partial deposits. Verify the agency has a valid Ministry of Tourism approval number. Search the agency name plus 'scam' or 'review' before booking. Pay by credit card for chargeback protection if the service is never delivered.
scams.location: Near Chennai Airport, Egmore area, online agencies targeting Chennai visitors
